verdict.rationale: FireHydrant documents its own MTTX Analytics page, which visualizes metrics for overall health and lets you filter or group by team, service, severity and similar fields. A separate Alerting Analytics page tracks events-to-alerts, acknowledgments and alerts-to-incidents, which partly covers incident and alert load. However, the quotes never explicitly name MTTA or MTTR, never show trends over time, and say nothing about on-call health. Missing for 10: explicit MTTA/MTTR metric definitions, time-series trend views showing improvement, on-call health metrics (pages per responder, off-hours load, burnout), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I get reliability analytics — MTTA/MTTR trends, incident load, on-call health — to see whether we are actually improving

citations.quote: This Analytics page groups and visualizes these metrics so you can understand overall health by entities like teams, impacted services, and more.
FireHydrant's analytics offer the ability to filter and group by various aspects... Service, Environment, Functionality, Team, Severity, User, [Custom Field]
Use our new Alerting Analytics page to understand how incoming events are turning into Alerts, how many alerts are being acknowledged, and how many alerts are then turning into incidents.
